about: Proposed marks for steps of the TD-1 bank, for the BCBA's approval. Nothing here is applied. tools/banks/mark-proposals.md is the readable copy.

items.card: Reward finished instructions with a break plus a preferred item, then thin the work requirement
items.text: Ignore any problem behavior that occurs during the break, and present the next instruction when the break ends.

items.card: End the meal early when the student feeds themselves the offered bites or drinks
items.text: Give no coaxing, reprimands or other reaction to pushing away, turning away, covering the mouth, crying, coughing or gagging.

items.card: Brief on-topic conversation for appropriate talk, none for off-topic or sexual remarks
items.text: Give no attention after an inappropriate statement and wait for the next appropriate one.

items.card: Answer appropriate talk with brief attention and give none for disruptive talk
items.text: Give no attention, comment or look of concern after disruptive vocalizations, and keep working.

items.card: Reinforce following simple requests, which also lowered untreated problem behavior
items.text: Give no reaction to aggression, disruption, property destruction or pica (no statements of concern), using only the least intrusive self-protection if the student hits.

items.card: Cue-pause-point with praise for answering instead of echoing (attention-maintained immediate echolalia)
items.text: When the student repeats any part of your words, withhold all attention until the student has gone 3 s without echoing; end the session after 9 such trials to avoid evoking problem behavior.

items.card: All-positive classroom plan: frequent praise, varied rewards and a daily reward menu
items.text: Stop reprimands and other negative consequences, and ignore minor misbehavior that is safe to ignore.

items.card: Preferred toys and play for 30 s after each accepted bite, to treat food refusal
items.text: Give no toys or attention after head turning, pushing the spoon or covering the mouth; in the first phase, remove the bite for 30 s and then present the next bite.

items.card: Praise for good table behavior and planned ignoring of disruption at meals
items.text: Give no attention to disruption; if head banging or other unsafe behavior occurs, follow the student's safety plan instead of ignoring it.

items.card: Parent praise for cooperative play and for following instructions, with planned ignoring of minor problem behavior
items.text: Ignore minor problem behavior: make no comment and do not turn to look when it happens.

items.card: Teach a "please" sign, then answer only the sign instead of reaching, grabbing or leading
items.text: When the student reaches, grabs, leads or yells, do not give the item; stay available and wait up to 30 s for the sign.

items.card: Attention for an early signal that comes before self-injury, and no attention for the self-injury
items.text: Give no comment, reprimand or other new attention for self-injury; if it happens while attention is already under way, finish only the planned 5 to 10 s.

items.card: Preferred-food bite and praise for accepting target foods at meals
items.text: Ignore spitting out, crying and pushing the spoon away; give no attention or extra food for them.

items.card: Preferred food or drink after each accepted bite (without escape extinction) for selective or low food intake
items.text: After a refusal or disruptive mealtime behavior, give no attention and no preferred item, and do not force the bite.

items.card: Give the wanted toy when the student reaches for it, never after self-injury
items.text: When head hitting occurs, do not hand over a toy; wait for a reach.

items.card: Red/green card game with points toward a class reward for attention-maintained classroom problem behavior
items.text: Tell the class the student is playing a game to earn a reward for everyone, and ask classmates to help by ignoring problem behavior.

items.card: Red/green card game with points toward a class reward for attention-maintained classroom problem behavior
items.text: When problem behavior occurs, turn the card to red and do not talk to, look at, or reprimand the student.

items.card: Give the item for a polite request, then build waiting up to 5 minutes before it comes
items.text: Give no access to the item after aggression or disruption.

items.card: Posted rules, praise for appropriate behavior and planned ignoring of minor disruption
items.text: Ignore disruptive behavior that is safe to ignore (leaving the seat, calling out, noises, turning around): no reminders, scolding or warnings.

items.card: Praise and a toy each time the student drinks from the cup within 8 seconds
items.text: Give no reaction (no coaxing, reprimands or comments) to pushing, throwing or turning away, and do not replace a thrown or dumped cup until the next scheduled drink.

items.card: Structured meal with praise and a toy for accepting bites (mild food selectivity)
items.text: Withhold attention for coughing, gagging, crying and hitting during the meal, following the nurse's guidance on when gagging or vomiting needs a response.

items.card: Teacher praise for task-relevant behavior with planned ignoring and a desk signal light
items.text: Ignore disruptive behavior that is safe to ignore.

items.card: Caution card: DRO still worked with some mixed errors but failed at 40% fidelity or less
items.text: Give nothing right after the target behavior, even when it would end the behavior quickly.

items.card: Resetting DRO with a chosen reward for staying close and walking during walks
items.text: After any elopement, dropping or attempt, restart the timer from the beginning, give no reprimands or statements of concern, and repeat "You need to walk with me."

items.card: Praise after each 15 minutes free of head hitting and screaming, built up from short sessions to the whole day
items.text: When head hitting or screaming occurs, give no attention for it; if it becomes dangerous, follow the student's crisis plan.

items.card: Whole-period quiet points in place of point fines for calling out and talking
items.text: During the period, ignore inappropriate verbalizations and do not take points away; keep a mental or written note of who spoke out.

items.card: Resetting DRO: attention after each interval free of self-injury, lengthened from session data
items.text: When self-injury occurs, give no attention and restart the interval timer.

items.card: DRO with attention and drinks for self-injury during free time
items.text: When self-injury or screaming occurs, do not talk to, touch or give a drink to the student at that moment, and start the period again.

items.card: Variable-momentary DRO: check at unpredictable times and reinforce if the behavior is not happening
items.text: Give no attention or item after self-injury at any other time; let the interval run to its end.

items.card: Variable-momentary DRO with attention for rare, intense aggression
items.text: Give no attention after aggression at any other time, and follow the student's crisis plan to keep everyone safe.

items.card: Whole-interval DRO to reduce behavior, then momentary DRO to maintain the reduction
items.text: Do not respond to the target behavior during the interval.

items.card: DRO for attention-maintained self-injury, with attention always withheld after self-injury
items.text: When self-injury occurs, give no attention of any kind (no concern, comments or redirection) and restart the 15-s timer.

items.card: DRO for attention-maintained self-injury, with attention always withheld after self-injury
items.text: Check that every adult near the student withholds attention after self-injury, because DRO without this step did not work even with 8 highly preferred items.

items.card: Delay after a request, with the other preferred reinforcer offered during the wait
items.text: Do not answer a request that does not match the current situation, and give no reaction to aggression.

items.card: Ask with a picture card, then wait for a larger amount while a timer runs
items.text: Answer each request with the item and give no food or TV after aggression.

items.card: After a request, have the student finish short tasks while waiting, adding tasks gradually
items.text: Teach the request first: remove the item or attention, prompt the request after 5 s, and give 30 s of the tablet or of play and talk for each request while problem behavior earns nothing.

items.card: After a request, have the student finish short tasks while waiting, adding tasks gradually
items.text: Give no item or attention for problem behavior during the wait; keep prompting the task (tangible function) or simply wait (attention function).

items.card: The waiting game in class: wait with other toys, a star token for each wait, three stars for a prize, waits lengthened to 5 min
items.text: If self-injury or aggression occurs, end the trial, follow the safety plan and give no item; start again after 10 s calm.

items.card: After a request, ask for a growing, varied number of tasks before the reward comes
items.text: Do not give the item after problem behavior; wait for the request and the tasks.

items.card: Room management for a group: one adult keeps everyone supplied with materials and prompts their use while a second works 5 min with each person in turn
items.text: Room manager: give no attention to inappropriate behavior, and leave alone whoever is working with the helper.

items.card: Free access to toys or an enriched area, plus a matched procedure per function
items.text: Where self-injury persists with attention, give 5 s of attention after each interval without self-injury and ignore self-injury, starting at 15 s and lengthening to 30, 60 and then 120 s as it stays low.

items.card: Choose the easiest request form so it wins out over aggression for toys
items.text: Withhold the toys after aggression and wait for a request before giving them again.

items.card: Functional communication training to ask to be left alone or ask for toys, with scheduled free access
items.text: Keep talking and commenting when problem behavior occurs, and do not give the preferred toy after problem behavior.

items.card: Give the other functional reinforcer while the requested one is delayed after FCT
items.text: Give no reprimand, attention or tablet after problem behavior.

items.card: Functional communication training with prompt delay for break or attention requests
items.text: Ignore self-injury maintained by attention and continue the activity.

items.card: Ask for attention with a red/green availability board (attention-maintained vomiting, gagging and related behavior)
items.text: Ignore every challenging behavior in the response class (vomiting, gagging, aggression, self-injury, disruption, verbal aggression and the rest) with no statements of concern; keep any clean-up brief and silent.

items.card: Functional communication training for attention, with a student-choice check among approved packages
items.text: Give no reprimands or statements of concern after problem behavior, and keep working on your own task.

items.card: FCT with a picture card for the type of attention the student prefers, chosen by a rapid attention-type assessment
items.text: Give no attention for problem behavior; from session 61 the study added 30 s of planned ignoring after each problem behavior, after which a card still on the green side could be exchanged.

items.card: FCT for attention-maintained behavior using the kind of attention a quick parent-run assessment shows the student prefers
items.text: Give no attention after problem behavior.

items.card: Brief functional analysis followed by giving the maintaining consequence for a simple request
items.text: When aggression is maintained by attention or a preferred item, ignore it (no consequence).

items.card: Functional communication training to ask for attention only when the adult is free
items.text: Give no attention for problem behavior and carry on with the current activity.

items.card: FCT with a card exchange for severe destructive behavior maintained by items: longer treatment alone does not prevent resurgence
items.text: Do not give the items for destructive behavior; if a card exchange comes within 3 s after destructive behavior, wait for the next exchange that is free of destructive behavior before reinforcing.

items.card: Card-exchange requests for items, with a written plan for lapses in answering them
items.text: If a lapse happens, keep withholding the item after destructive behavior, resume answering the card as soon as possible, and log the lapse.

items.card: Card-exchange FCT taught with a progressive prompt delay, then held on a lean variable-interval schedule for many sessions to limit relapse
items.text: Give nothing for problem behavior, and if it occurs within 3 s of a card response, wait for a new card response with 3 s clear before honoring it.

items.card: FCT in short trials: picture-card request for a toy or a break, taught by a parent coached by video
items.text: Teaching trials: immediately prompt the student to touch the card; give the toy back, or remove the work, for the rest of the minute; give nothing for problem behavior.

items.card: Thin a card request by taking the card out of reach for growing periods
items.text: When aggression occurs, do not give the attention or the items for it, and continue the activity.

items.card: Start functional communication training with a request card, then shift it step by step to a spoken request
items.text: When problem behavior occurs, give nothing, wait 3 s with no problem behavior, then prompt the request.

items.card: Functional communication training with competing items within reach while requests are thinned
items.text: Give no attention or item after problem behavior.

items.card: Caution card: longer FCT alone does not prevent relapse when requests go unanswered
items.text: Withhold the item after destructive behavior, and if destructive behavior came right before a request, wait for the next request with none before answering.

items.card: Functional communication training that honors every request when extinction is not always possible
items.text: Do not give the reinforcer after problem behavior whenever it can safely be withheld.

items.card: Functional communication training that also gives other liked items with the requested reinforcer (combined reinforcers), with the student's preference checked
items.text: Give no reaction to problem behavior, and do not reinforce a request that comes within 5 s after problem behavior.

items.card: Functional communication training: asking for a more suitable garment instead of self-injury
items.text: Do not give the item after self-injury, and stay calm and continue the session.

items.card: Functional communication training: asking 'Am I doing good work?' to get adult attention
items.text: Ignore challenging behavior and keep the planned schedule of praise and directions going.

items.card: Functional communication training with a picture-card touch that staff can guide, before a spoken request
items.text: For attention-maintained behavior, give no attention for problem behavior and stay with the other activity until the next trial.

items.card: Three treatments matched to a brief assessment: timed attention plus a taught hand raise, a food request offered after every task trial, and leisure items when alone
items.text: Give no reaction to challenging behavior in any of the three.

items.card: Functional communication training on a lean schedule, run longer, to limit relapse when requests go unanswered
items.text: Give nothing for problem behavior, and if it occurs within 3 s of a request, wait for a new request with 3 s free of problem behavior before giving the item or attention.

items.card: Major problem behavior: extinction plus prompting an appropriate way to ask, and following through on demands
items.text: When major problem behavior occurs, do not give the preferred item, activity or extra attention that it was getting.

items.card: Pick the replacement request from the first appropriate response seen during extinction
items.text: Give no programmed consequence for other responses or for problem behavior.

items.card: Teach two new request forms, then let the student pick the one they prefer
items.text: Give 60 s of attention or of the item after each request, and give nothing for problem behavior while the reinforcer is unavailable.

items.card: Finding the preferred way to ask by placing request forms on extinction one at a time within FCT
items.text: Run 5-min FCT sessions with all three forms available, give 30 s with the preferred item after every request in any form, and do not give the item after problem behavior.

items.card: FCT with several request modes taught, then the preferred mode placed on extinction in turn
items.text: After challenging behavior, withhold the item and keep attention low; give no attention during the 30-s access, and do not honor a request that comes within 3 s of challenging behavior.

items.card: Functional communication training, then thinning with signaled answer and wait periods
items.text: Give no reaction to problem behavior and continue the session.

items.card: Parent-run FCT with a picture card at home after a coached brief functional analysis, for toddlers
items.text: Give nothing for problem behavior, and wait until it has stopped for at least 3 s before prompting the card.

items.card: Functional communication training: hand a picture card to get adult attention
items.text: Give no attention after hitting, kicking, pinching or scratching, and continue the session.

items.card: Functional communication training: ask for play with a phrase or a card, with no attention for destructive behavior
items.text: Give no attention or other reaction to destructive behavior and keep the session going.

items.card: Teach young students to ask "play with me" or "toys please" during classroom play
items.text: Give no attention and no toys after aggression or property destruction.

items.card: Function-based replacement behavior training in general education: teach and reinforce a replacement that gets the same outcome, run by the teacher
items.text: Honor the replacement right away at first; problem behavior no longer gets the outcome.

items.card: FCT to ask for missing puzzle pieces or rings to be put back, for problem behavior maintained by restoring the arrangement
items.text: After that, prompt only after an error; give no restoration after problem behavior.

items.card: Caution card: which FCT changes lessened the return of problem behavior when requests went unanswered
items.text: Give no reinforcer for problem behavior during FCT.

items.card: Functional communication training that gives the request a longer, richer reinforcer than problem behavior
items.text: Ignore milder problem behavior such as crying or throwing toys.

items.card: Functional communication training for aggression when a routine or arrangement is disrupted, with fast delay thinning
items.text: Give no access to the item after aggression, and continue the session.

items.card: Functional communication with a card touch, using short 20-second reinforcer periods
items.text: In toy sessions, give no toys after self-injury or aggression.

items.card: Functional communication training with a sign, extinction and a gradually longer work requirement
items.text: For item-maintained behavior, do not hand over the item after problem behavior; give it only after the student signs.

items.card: Replace crying and whining with a sign for attention, toys or being picked up
items.text: Give no attention, toys or contact for crying or whining, after checking that basic needs are met.

items.card: Teach separate requests for attention and toys, each honored only while its picture is posted
items.text: Give no attention, reprimand or toys after destructive behavior and continue the activity.

items.card: Functional communication training thinned with signals showing when requests will be honored
items.text: Honor every request and give no reinforcer for destructive behavior; if it occurs just as the reinforcer is due, wait 3 to 5 s before giving it.

items.card: FCT with a cardboard keyguard over a speech device so a blind student can feel the buttons (break, eat, tickles), for self-injury with several functions
items.text: Give nothing for self-injury.

items.card: Teach an "I want to talk" card in place of aggression for favorite topics
items.text: Give no conversation or other attention after aggression, and keep the student and others safe.

items.card: FCT for toy-maintained aggression with a picture card or button, before fixed-lean schedule thinning
items.text: Do not give the toys after aggression or property destruction.

items.card: FCT for two functions in turn: "I want (item) please" for preferred items and "I need help please" for hard tasks, with the wait raised from 2 s to 5 s
items.text: If self-injury or aggression occurs, give no item or help, prompt the phrase, and honor it.

items.card: Teach two ways to ask for a preferred item so a back-up request comes back before problem behavior
items.text: Give no item after aggression or after the other request form.

items.card: Teach a separate request for each function: a want sign for items, a break or help card for hard work
items.text: After problem behavior in this condition, withhold the item and prompt the item request.

items.card: Functional communication training with wristband signals that carry to new rooms and staff
items.text: Give 20 s with the items and praise for each request, and give no items after problem behavior; for a student who does not use the rule, prompt "Say '[item] please'" after a wait that grows from 0 s to 2 s, 5 s and 10 s.

items.card: Whole-class favorite game for few call-outs, plus praise for hand raising
items.text: Answer only students who raise their hands, and do not respond to call-outs.

items.card: Whole-class favorite game for few call-outs, plus praise for hand raising
items.text: When counts stay low, keep praising hand raising and ignoring call-outs; in the second-grade class this alone kept call-outs low in the last week of school.

items.card: Class-wide attention signal, visual transition timer and group reward for on-time transitions
items.text: Throughout the day, praise on-task students and those who raise their hands, ignore minor misbehavior, and use proximity or gestures with students who continue.

items.card: Set and thin the free-access schedule from the student's own time between behaviors
items.cite: Kahng et al., 2000a; Goh et al., 2000
items.text: Give no reinforcer right after self-injury.

items.card: Stay close and give attention every 30 s to prevent attention-maintained elopement
items.text: Give no preferred items or activities after elopement.

items.card: Give attention on a time schedule matched to how often the student asked for it
items.text: Give no attention or other reaction to destructive behavior.

items.card: Attention every 30 s at times when warning signs of a mood episode appear
items.text: Give no added attention for aggression, property destruction or leaving the area, and keep giving the scheduled comments.

items.card: Scheduled attention, thinned from continuous to every 5 minutes, for attention-maintained aggression
items.text: Give no attention after aggression or disruption, and carry on with the activity without comment.

items.card: Continuous noncontingent attention during play for attention-maintained destructive behavior
items.text: Keep the attention going in the same way when destructive behavior occurs, and do not reprimand or comment on it.

items.card: Give attention throughout the activity and ignore attention-seeking problem behavior
items.text: Do not change your attention after problem behavior: give no extra comment, look or reaction to it and continue the interaction as before.

items.card: Continuous noncontingent attention for attention-maintained self-injury that cannot be ignored
items.text: Give no reprimand or warning after self-injury; the study's reprimand ("Stop that or you will hurt yourself") raised self-injury to 12.8 per minute.

items.card: Dense time-based food delivery, with leisure items also available
items.text: Give no extra food after the target behavior.

items.card: Scheduled attention with staff seated at a distance where self-injury does not occur
items.text: Give no attention after self-injury, and delay the next scheduled delivery so that no attention comes within 10 s after an instance.

items.card: Give attention on a clock that slowly thins, instead of ignoring problem behavior
items.text: Give no attention for property destruction, self-injury or tantrums between scheduled deliveries.

items.card: Timed teacher attention on a fixed schedule to reduce talking out in class
items.text: Answer appropriate hand-raised questions about the work quickly and briefly, and do not respond to other talking out.

items.card: Noncontingent delivery of the maintaining item in a large enough amount per delivery
items.text: Give nothing extra after the target behavior.

items.card: Timed free access to a preferred item, starting at the baseline latency
items.text: Give no reaction and no item after problem behavior between rings.

items.card: Continuous access to a top preferred item in place of attention when staff are busy
items.text: Make no response to destructive behavior.

items.card: Give 15 minutes of steady conversation before times when adults cannot attend
items.text: During the period, stay in the room but give no attention for problem behavior.

items.card: Scheduled access to items or attention, with a spoken signal and timer for their return
items.text: Give no item or attention after problem behavior, and keep to the timer.

items.card: Scheduled free access to toys plus toys for each request, for tangible-maintained behavior
items.text: Give no toys, comments or other consequence after self-injury or aggression.

items.card: Free access on a dense schedule, thinned so the student's new request can grow
items.cite: Goh et al., 2000; Kahng et al., 2000a
items.text: Give the reinforcer on a fixed-time schedule set just below the mean time between self-injuries in baseline (FT 5 s in the study), whatever the student is doing, and give nothing right after self-injury.

items.card: Free access to the maintaining reinforcer every 5 minutes from the first session, with extinction
items.text: Give no attention or item after problem behavior, and carry on with the session as before.

items.card: Caution card: run noncontingent reinforcement on a varied schedule because missed deliveries matter
items.text: Give no reinforcer right after problem behavior.

items.card: Give the preferred item on a varying time schedule, thinned to about every 5 minutes
items.text: Give no item after problem behavior, and keep to the timed list.

items.card: Noncontingent reinforcement with extinction kept in place, to limit return of behavior later
items.text: Give nothing after the target behavior itself, so the behavior no longer produces the item.

items.card: Move from answering requests to time-based delivery at the same rate, so problem behavior does not come back
items.text: Deliver the reinforcer on that fixed-time schedule (in the study, 1 or 2 s after each 30-s access period ended), whether or not the student asks, and give no planned response to problem behavior.

items.card: Peer buddies trained to run a function-based support plan during the PE routine
items.text: If the student drops to the ground, have the peers move away and withhold attention until she is redirected, then attend again as soon as she walks; follow the school's safety procedure if challenging behavior lasts more than 30 s.

items.card: Popular classmates trained to ignore disruption and respond to rule-following
items.text: Tell the helpers to ignore rule-breaking completely and to respond warmly when the target student follows the rules.

items.card: High-school tutors trained by video, role-play and feedback to teach instruction following
items.text: Have the tutor turn away from crying, wandering or sitting on the floor and resume when the student is calm.

items.card: Trained classmates who check on, praise and record a peer's appropriate behavior, for classroom disruption
items.text: Teach the manager to ignore the target student's disruptive behavior: no looking, laughing, talking or arguing in response.

items.card: Teach the student to challenge a partner's false game rule while playing board games
items.text: Ignore whining about lost turns or payments and keep playing.

items.card: Fade self-held arm tubes to wrist bands with prompts and praise, to end self-restraint while keeping self-injury low
items.text: Give no attention for self-injury, and stop the session if the agreed injury level is reached.

items.card: Brief fixed-length time-out from play, ended on time without a calm-down requirement
items.text: During the activity, give no attention to problem behavior and keep the usual toys, games and peer play available.

items.card: Video replay of the problem behavior right before a delayed time-out
items.text: Give no attention or other consequence for tantrum behavior during the session; if the student stops working, tell them to keep working.

items.card: Teach a short "my way" request, then shape it into a polite, complete request
items.text: Give no student-led time for precursor or problem behavior; prompt the request instead.

items.card: Teach a simple, then a polite "Excuse me, may I have..." request for the toy and play
items.text: Give no item and no attention for problem behavior, and keep the trial going.

items.card: Offer another preferred task when a requested item is not available (caregiver guide)
items.text: If problem behavior occurs, do not hand over the unavailable item; follow the student's plan for major problem behavior.

items.card: Skill-based treatment in the classroom to bring back schoolwork after a long absence: request, tolerate the tablet being taken, then follow instructions
items.text: Give nothing for problem behavior, and run it within the class routine with the classroom staff.

items.card: Say no to a requested activity and offer a preferred alternative right away
items.text: Do not give the requested activity for any problem behavior, at any step of the escalation.

items.card: Chained schedule with a signaled adult-led link and student-led link for problem behavior maintained by adult compliance with nonvocal mands
items.text: During the student-led link, honor every request made with a picture card or sign right away, ignore grabbing, and ask what the student means when they only make a single-syllable sound so they can give a clearer request.

items.card: Say yes with a condition: the activity follows a short task
items.text: Give no response and no access to the activity for problem behavior during the task, and keep the same offer in place.

items.card: Make asking for an item pay off far more often than aggression
items.text: Withhold the item after aggression whenever it is safe to do so, and follow the crisis plan for safety.

items.card: Answer the student's request only after a set wait that lengthens to 5 minutes
items.text: Give no items or other consequence after tantrums.

items.card: When attention or toys cannot be given, post the picture for the other and honor that request
items.text: Give no attention, reprimand or toys after destructive behavior and continue the activity.

items.card: Signaled ask and wait periods, with adult play and talk during the wait periods
items.text: Give nothing for problem behavior in either period.

items.card: Use a bracelet on the adult's wrist to signal when requests will be honored
items.text: Give no planned consequence for problem behavior in either period.

items.card: Signal when requests are answered, then jump straight to a lean schedule
items.text: Run FCT at a rich schedule: give about 60 s with the preferred items, remove them, then answer every request with brief praise and 20 s with the items, and give nothing for problem behavior.

items.card: Fixed-lean multiple schedule (60 s green / 240 s red) to thin FCT for toys
items.text: Do not give the toys after problem behavior in either period.

items.card: Green and red request cards so problem behavior stays low when requests go unanswered
items.text: Give nothing for aggression or self-injury in either period, and hold back the item if problem behavior happened within 3 s before a request.

items.card: Noncontingent items in a multiple schedule: green card with free access, red card without, alternating every minute, then one minute of access in ten
items.text: Give no consequence for problem behavior in either component.

items.card: Request to go back to a ritual after it is interrupted, then red and green times, after a trial-based functional analysis
items.text: After each request, let the student go back to the ritual; give nothing for problem behavior.

items.card: Check whether the student can use a red-green signal before thinning requests with it
items.text: Give no planned consequence for problem behavior in either kind of session.

items.card: Start the full signaled wait with a competing activity, then fade the activity
items.text: Give no item for problem behavior at any time.

items.card: "Your way" and "my way" cards for repetitive speech: the adult answers each repetitive question while the green card is out, and redirects to other topics under the red card
items.text: Give no reply related to the repetitive speech after problem behavior, in either component.

items.card: Classwide lesson-by-lesson point ratings exchanged for prizes to reduce disruptive behavior
items.text: Praise rule-following often during lessons and ignore minor disruption that is safe to ignore.

items.card: Token economy with fines: buying back access and a fine payoff that grows with fine-free days
items.text: Prompt and reinforce behavior incompatible with the finable behaviors, and ignore minor problem behavior that carries no fine.

items.card: Token marks for each letter written, traded for home privileges (no clear effect in this study)
items.text: Keep ignoring problem behavior and praising work as set out in the attention plan used alongside the tokens.

items.card: Token ratings for following class rules every 15 minutes, faded to student self-ratings
items.text: Set a kitchen timer for 15 minutes; while it runs, help students one at a time with their reading, praise rule following and ignore minor disruption.

items.card: High-probability request sequence before household task requests
items.text: Keep the task in place when problem behavior occurs; do not leave or end the request because of it.

items.card: Teach new targets without mixing in mastered tasks, after a comparison of interspersal ratios
items.text: Continue the trial sequence when problem behavior occurs, without removing the materials or giving a break for it (escape extinction).

items.card: Steady paced instructions with praise for disruption that follows adult directions
items.text: When disruption occurs, give the next instruction on schedule; do not stop, turn away, remove the materials or wait longer before the next direction.

items.card: Repeated picture-and-word warnings before work starts or a liked item is shared
items.text: Give no item and no break after self-injury.
